segments.text: Good day, Mrs. Nováková. Come in.
What do you want to start with today?
Good day. I don't know. I feel like someone pulled my blanket under my leg.
What happened?
After 15 years of marriage, Radka and I have decided to divorce.
And I still can't understand it.
Tell me more.
We were still in Croatia last year. Everything looked normal.
And in September he told me that it's not possible anymore.
How did you accept it?
I was sitting in the kitchen and couldn't say anything.
Then I went to clean the dishes as if nothing was happening.
And what was inside you?
Empty. Then anger. Then again emptiness.
I'm telling you, Radek, why.
She says we pretended to live next to each other.
I didn't notice it or I didn't want to notice it.
What do you think about it now?
That I should have seen it, that I'm blind.
I keep looking back in my head where I made a mistake.
And your own?
No.
Sometimes I think I was too tired and I didn't care about it.
Sometimes I thought I was too much worried.
It seems you are suffering a lot in that hour.
Yes, mainly because of the kids.
Tell me about them.
I have two kids. Aniška is 12 and Matěj is 8 years old.
I don't know how to tell them.
You haven't told them yet?
No, Radek wants us to say it together, but we keep postponing it.
Anička is already thinking about something.
What did she say to you?
Last week she asked me if we were arguing with dad.
I said no. I felt terrible.
Why terrible?
Because I lied to her and she knew it. She saw it in my eyes.
What did you think about?
That I would ruin her life, that I would take her home.
How did you manage to tell her the truth?
I'd rather have it with me, but I'm afraid of their tears. Matěj is still a kid, he doesn't understand much.
What would you like to give him?
That we both like him and that it doesn't change.
But I don't know if it's true, when I don't know what it will look like.
What will it look like with the apartment?
The apartment is in the pharmacy, Radek is going to his brother, at least so far. The children will stay with me.
How do you feel about that?
I'm afraid I won't be able to do it.
I'm glad I always managed to earn money.
What do you do every day?
I work as a Czech teacher at a primary school in Brno.
I teach 9th and 8th graders.
How do you study now?
I go to class with a little boy in my lap.
I feel like everyone sees that my life is falling apart.
Does anyone know about it at school?
Only the teacher.
I told her that because I once cried at the dance.
She was nice.
What helped you?
That she let me go earlier.
She gave me a free hour.
But then I was sitting at home and it was worse.
Worse? Why?
Because I was alone at work.
I had to do something.
How do you sleep?
Badly.
Every night I wake up at 3 a.m. and think about what's next.
What do you say when you wake up?
That I don't have a mortgage,
I have no mortgage, no husband, nothing.
I count the money and imagine how I will tell my children.
It's all spinning.
And then?
I sleep around 5 and get up at 7.30.
I am tired already in the morning.
Do you eat? Do you move?
I don't eat much. I lost 4 kilos.
My friend tells me that I look terrible.
Do you have anyone you can talk to?
I have a sister in Olomouc. She calls me almost every evening. And my friend Eva from work.
What does she say?
She wants almost everything. Eva just wants me to have a hard time. She doesn't want me to think about anything.
What are you afraid of?
That I lied. That a woman who can't keep a marriage is not a good example for children.
That's a hard thought. Where does it come from?
Probably from my mum. She always said that marriage is a thing and that it's what it is.
What did she say when you introduced her?
She kept silent. Then she said that she hopes I've been good to her. She hasn't called me much since then.
How do you feel?
Sad. I need you to forgive me.
What would you like to say?
That it hurts, that I don't want to be alone, but that it doesn't work with us.
What happens when you say it out loud?
I cry and I apologize.
It's not for nothing. Take your time.
Thank you. I haven't told anyone yet.
What's wrong with you? That you said it here?
It's strange to sit here and say it all out loud. But it helps a little.
What could help you the most?
Sleep. And you, grandpa, how to say it to your children?
Let's go step by step.
What about sleeping? Have you tried anything?
German tea and that's all. Doctor offered me some powder, but I don't want to.
Why don't you want it?
I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to wake up for my children in time and I don't want to be dependent.
I see.
Would you try to sit next to the bed and write down what wakes you up?
I could. At least I'll get it out of my head.
And what about children? What are you most afraid of?
That I'll panic and cry. That I won't be able to stay calm.
So you wouldn't mind?
That I'd be scared of children? That it would be scary for them?
Or they could see that the sadness is allowed.
I didn't think so. And she's not sensitive. Maybe it would help her.
We can see how to prepare it next time. What are you going to do today?
That I'm not alone and I don't have to do it right away.
Exactly. That's it for today.
Thank you. See you next week.
